what: Expected verdict mix for 1,000,000 URLs vs true phishing prevalence, default vs --base-rate=prevalence (safe mode). Counts are expectations: N_class x measured per-class verdict share.

model.rule: FRAUD if p >= th_fraud and p_adj >= 0.5; LEGITIMATE if p <= th_legit and p_adj <= 0.5; else REVIEW (fraudurl/cli.py score_rows); p_adj = Model.adjust_prior(p, base_rate)

why_central: newest data (2026-06-26 to 2026-09-25), i.e. the phishing and web of the year the tool is used; phishing from openphish_history, phishtank_online_valid
mixed legitimate side (hackernews_30d, commoncrawl_2026_tranco) with 20.1% bare homepages, between PhreshPhish (9.9%) and a homepage list (100%)
its legitimate->FRAUD rate 1.78% (domain-bootstrap 95% CI 1.23%-2.38%) agrees with the fully external Ariyadasa collection (1.85%, CI 1.66%-2.04%), which never contributed training data
caveats_central: small: 2,355 legitimate and 2,363 phishing test URLs (3,844 domains), so the false-alarm count at low prevalence is uncertain by about +-32%
fresh26 carries 35% of the training weight (other domains, same collection method), so its rates may be slightly optimistic for a batch collected in a different way
its legitimate side is links posted to Hacker News and Common Crawl pages of popular domains - more tech/blog content than e.g. an e-mail gateway log

best_case.why: lowest legitimate->FRAUD rate (0.29%) and REVIEW share of legitimate URLs (16.6%); real browsing telemetry, but PhreshPhish is 55% of the training weight, so this is the model's home distribution and an optimistic bound

false_alarms_and_REVIEW.why: bare homepages of popular sites: 2.61% of them FRAUD and 76.5% REVIEW

missed_phishing_and_FRAUD_capture.why: 2020-era data: 4.9% of phishing called LEGITIMATE and only 55.7% reaches FRAUD; among 2026-era external phishing, JPCERT (57.4% to FRAUD, 2.0% to LEGITIMATE) is the weakest
